key_insight: Differentiable foundation models enable joint optimization of crystal composition and structure toward target properties, including band gaps for photovoltaic absorbers.
engineering_relevance: This approach could accelerate solar-absorber candidate discovery by optimizing electronic properties while penalizing energetically unfavorable structures.
method: DEFEAT extends pretrained EquiformerV3 to continuous species weights and site occupancies without fractional-data retraining.
Property-model gradients and a learned energy penalty jointly update composition, atom count, atomic positions, and lattice vectors.
SCAN calculations evaluate photovoltaic candidates against a 1.34 eV band-gap target and DFT stability.
evidence_signal: SCAN calculations confirmed ten novel structures with gaps within 20% of the target on their respective raw or empirically corrected scales, all within 70 meV/atom of the DFT hull.
watch_item: Training-functional band-gap bias propagates into designs unless corrected in the objective; target gaps alone do not establish solar-cell performance.
paper_title: Inverse design of superconductors and semiconductors with differentiable foundation models
